test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A tank was filled with 300 ltr of water. During the day 87 ltr 225 ml of water was used. How much water was left in the tank at the end of the day?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the **milliliters** first by borrowing 1 **ltr** (1000 ml) from the **total capacity**.

1000 ml − 225 ml = 775 ml

299 ltr − 87 ltr = 212 ltr

Result: 212 ltr 775 ml

**∴ The correct answer is 212 ltr 775 ml.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial quantity of water in tank = 300 ltr

Quantity of water used = 87 ltr 225 ml

**Formula Used:**

**Water left** = **Total water** − **Used water**

1 liter = 1000 milliliters

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a48b9ba23c103970ac9e739917994f1b69054640a17c6154d40a476fece97ba.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total water = 300.000 ltr

⇒ Used water = 87.225 ltr

⇒ Water left = 300.000 − 87.225

⇒ Water left = 212.775 ltr

⇒ 212.775 ltr = 212 ltr 775 ml

**∴ The correct answer is 212 ltr 775 ml.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Metric Conversion

Standard unit of volume is **liters**. 1 Liter (L) = 1000 Milliliters (ml). To convert L to ml, multiply by 1000.

Subtraction with Units

When subtracting mixed units, subtract the smaller units first. If the upper value is smaller, **borrow** 1 unit from the larger category (e.g., borrow 1 ltr to get 1000 ml).</p
